clue.text: Jack as Ensign Beverley, unrestricted

definitions.meaning: in Sheridan's The Rivals, Captain Jack wooes Lydia Languish disguised as the penniless Ensign Beverley; his surname is the answer

explanation.surface: A man named Jack poses as a junior officer and acts without any restraint.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheridan's hero Captain Jack takes this surname, and the adjective also means complete or limitless.

clue.text: Outspoken porter deceives Potter?

indicators.note: spoken out loud, so the phrase that follows is said and its sound gives the entry

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, and deceives means tricks

explanation.surface: A loud-mouthed railway porter is fooling someone who makes pots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potter' looks like a maker of pottery, but it is the surname of the children's author and illustrator of Peter Rabbit; the question mark flags the name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Peter Rabbit author was Miss Potter, whose first name this is.

clue.text: Carel Fisher's housekeeper lover's ending in cold soil, sadly

indicators.note: sadly suggests the letters have been put in a sorry, disordered state and must be rearranged
ending tells us to take only the final letter of lover's

explanation.surface: A housekeeper mourns her lover, whose life ended buried in cold earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges R (the last letter of lover's) with COLDSOIL. In Iris Murdoch's The Time of the Angels, the rector Carel Fisher's housekeeper and mistress is Pattie O'Driscoll.
explanation.definitionFit: Pattie bearing this surname keeps house for the Reverend Carel Fisher in Murdoch's novel The Time of the Angels.

clue.text: Latin American sport taken up by a Hero's attendant

indicators.note: in a down clue, taken up means the letters are read upwards, back to front

parts.note: US abbreviates American, as in United States
RU stands for Rugby Union, a sport

explanation.surface: A South American game is adopted by the servant of a heroic figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken up' turns the three short pieces around before A is added. 'Hero' is not a brave man but the heroine of Much Ado About Nothing, whose gentlewoman this is.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's Much Ado About Nothing, the gentlewoman serving Hero bears this name.

clue.text: US biographer, journalist and general learns to catch fish

indicators.note: to catch means the string of other pieces holds the fish inside it, here just after the first piece

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is the crossword journalist
Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general
masters means learns thoroughly
a gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: An American writer, newsman and military commander is learning how to land a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spoon River Anthology poet also wrote biographies of Lincoln, Whitman and Twain, hence 'biographer'.
explanation.definitionFit: The American poet of Spoon River Anthology also published life stories of Lincoln, Twain and Whitman.

clue.text: Saul, caretaker of Cruella's tot, tucked into cake

annotationWithheld.why: Saul, caretaker of Cruella's tot, tucked into cake (6): cold solve's guess BURDEN fits the crossings but no parse found for 'caretaker of Cruella's tot' or for Saul as definition
annotationWithheld.clue: Saul, caretaker of Cruella's tot, tucked into cake

clue.text: "Now, gods, stand up for -!" (King Lear)

parts.note: the missing word completes Edmund's soliloquy in King Lear, Act 1 Scene 2, where the illegitimate son defends his kind

explanation.surface: A quotation from Shakespeare with its final word left blank.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund, the illegitimate son of Gloucester, ends his speech calling on the gods to champion those born out of wedlock.

clue.text: A bold novel about India opener in our top game

indicators.note: about means going around, so the rearranged letters surround the next piece
novel means new or fresh, so the letters of A bold are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: opener in our points to the first letter of the word our

explanation.surface: A daring new book about India begins with our country's favourite game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges A BOLD to DABOL, which goes 'about' I to make DIABOL; 'opener' then adds the O from our. 'top' is not best but a spinning toy: in diabolo you spin a two-cupped top on a string held between two sticks.
explanation.definitionFit: Diabolo is a juggling game in which an hourglass-shaped spinning top is whirled on a string.

clue.text: Spare a husband and beat up Bartholomew, possibly

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the whole string is read from bottom to top, back to front

parts.note: spare means thin, lean
to tan someone is to beat them

explanation.surface: Skinny and married, someone gives Bartholomew a thrashing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns LEANAHTAN round. Tradition identifies the apostle Bartholomew with the Nathanael of John's Gospel, hence 'possibly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Many scholars think the apostle Bartholomew is the same man John's Gospel calls Nathanael, though the link is uncertain.

clue.text: Munich writer in part of Scotland

definitions.meaning: Robert ... wrote the 2017 thriller Munich, about the 1938 agreement
an island region of the Outer Hebrides, joined to Lewis

explanation.surface: An author from the Bavarian capital lives somewhere in the Highlands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Munich' is not the writer's home city but the title of a Robert Harris novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Harris wrote the novel Munich, and Harris is also the southern part of the Hebridean island Lewis and Harris.

clue.text: Maybe Saturn's chat with Atlas?

definitions.note: Saturn's is read as Saturn is, so the definition is an example of a type of planet

parts.note: gas is idle talk, chatter
Atlas was a Titan, a giant who held up the sky

explanation.surface: Is this what the god Saturn says when gossiping with the Titan Atlas?
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Saturn's stands for 'is'. The surface pictures two Titans of myth chatting; the answer is the planet type.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturn, like Jupiter, is a huge planet made mostly of hydrogen and helium rather than rock.

clue.text: Millhauser's dreamer left trapped by backstage assistant

indicators.note: trapped by means the next piece is held inside the assistant's word

parts.note: a dresser helps actors with costumes behind the scenes

explanation.surface: A novelist's dreamer is left stuck with a theatre helper.
explanation.walkthrough: Steven Millhauser's Pulitzer-winning novel is Martin Dressler: The Tale of an American Dreamer.
explanation.definitionFit: Millhauser subtitled his novel about the hotel builder Martin the Tale of an American Dreamer.

clue.text: King wearing gold — gold found by a goddess

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold
R, for Rex, is the abbreviation for king
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A monarch decked in gold finds more gold beside a goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' puts R inside AU.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman deity of the dawn bears this name.

clue.text: He killed King Richard by infiltrating a school

indicators.note: infiltrating means getting inside, so one piece is put into the school

parts.note: Eton is a famous English public school
by gives X, the multiplication sign, as in three by four

explanation.surface: A regicide got into a school to murder the king.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's Richard II, Sir Piers of Exton murders the deposed king at Pomfret Castle.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Piers of Exton kills the deposed Richard II at Pomfret in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: Topaz, an innocent traveller is bound to value

parts.note: a bound is a boundary or edge
worth means value

explanation.surface: A gemstone and a naive tourist are destined to be prized.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topaz' is not the gem: Ethel Wilson's novel The Innocent Traveller follows Topaz Edgeworth through a long life.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethel Wilson's novel The Innocent Traveller centres on Topaz, whose family name this is.

clue.text: A maiden ended so tragically

indicators.note: tragically suggests ruin, so the letters are wrecked and rearranged

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A young woman's life came to a sad end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tragically' rearranges A, M and ENDEDSO. The whole clue also describes Othello's young wife, smothered by her husband.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello's young bride is murdered by her jealous husband, a tragic end for an innocent girl.

clue.text: German composer's school, housed by a miser

definitions.note: composer's is read as composer is

indicators.note: housed by means the school is lodged inside the miser's name

parts.note: Silas Marner is George Eliot's miser

explanation.surface: A German composer's academy is lodged with a skinflint.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of composer's stands for 'is'. Heinrich Marschner wrote German Romantic operas such as Der Vampyr.
explanation.definitionFit: Heinrich Marschner was a nineteenth-century German writer of Romantic operas.

clue.text: Irish poet spots complaint being hidden by timid types

indicators.note: being hidden by means the complaint is tucked inside the timid types

parts.note: mice are proverbially timid
acne is a skin complaint of spots

explanation.surface: An Irish poet notices that shy people are concealing their grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spots' looks like a verb meaning sees; it describes the complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis MacNeice was a Belfast-born poet of the 1930s generation.

clue.text: Game I play with Lulu Apollinaire?

indicators.note: play suggests the letters are played with, moved about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A game invented to play with Wedekind's Lulu and the French poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' rearranges GAMEI and LULU. The question mark flags that only the poet's first name is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: The French poet who wrote Alcools was christened Guillaume Apollinaire, so this is his given name.

clue.text: UN arts sponsor uses satellite to put out its first avant-garde dramatist

indicators.note: to put out its first means the opening letter of the sponsor is expelled and the satellite takes its place

parts.note: UNESCO is the UN body for education, science and culture
Io is a moon of Jupiter

explanation.surface: A United Nations culture body uses a satellite to promote an experimental playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: Replacing U in UNESCO with the Jupiter moon IO gives the Romanian-French author of The Bald Soprano and Rhinoceros.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugene Ionesco was a leading figure of the Theatre of the Absurd.

clue.text: Poetry book a college doesn't open

indicators.note: doesn't open means the college loses its opening letter

parts.note: Oriel is a college of Oxford University

explanation.surface: A book of verse that one college won't start reading.
explanation.walkthrough: Sylvia Plath's posthumous 1965 collection has the same name as the spirit in The Tempest.
explanation.definitionFit: Sylvia Plath's best-known collection of verse, published after her death, bears this title.

clue.text: "Sage of Concord" LP released by ELP?

indicators.note: released by means these letters are let go from the band's name, leaving the rest

parts.note: ELP is the rock band ..., Lake and Palmer
here LP stands for the band's other two members

explanation.surface: An album by a prog-rock trio pays tribute to a New England philosopher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'LP' looks like a long-playing record, but it is the L and P of ELP: Lake and Palmer. Release them and Emerson is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph Waldo Emerson, the transcendentalist essayist, lived in Concord, Massachusetts and was known by that nickname.

clue.text: A writer at heart, adored very much

indicators.note: at heart means the central letters of adored are taken

parts.note: well means thoroughly, very much

explanation.surface: A novelist is, at bottom, greatly loved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at heart' takes OR, the middle two letters of adored.
explanation.definitionFit: George Orwell, author of Nineteen Eighty-Four, is a writer.

clue.text: Dirt Music author with popular style

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
ton means fashion or style

explanation.surface: An Australian novelist writes with a popular touch.
explanation.walkthrough: Tim Winton is the Australian author of Dirt Music and Cloudstreet.
explanation.definitionFit: Tim Winton, the Western Australian novelist, wrote Dirt Music.

clue.text: Biographer and genius's last attempt to conceal pain

indicators.note: last points to the final letter of genius's
to conceal means the attempt hides the pain inside it

parts.note: a try is an attempt
an ache is a pain

explanation.surface: A biographer and a brilliant mind make a final effort to hide their suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: Lytton Strachey wrote Eminent Victorians and Queen Victoria.
explanation.definitionFit: Lytton Strachey reinvented the life story with Eminent Victorians.

clue.text: Princess of France's attendant men returned bearing salt

indicators.note: returned means the men's letters are sent back, read in reverse

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers, men
saline means salt, salty

explanation.surface: The French princess's servants come back with salt.
explanation.walkthrough: In Love's Labour's Lost, Rosaline is one of the ladies attending the Princess of France.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosaline is a lady-in-waiting to the Princess of France in Love's Labour's Lost.

clue.text: Wise, perhaps, to ignore one street in Worthing

indicators.note: to ignore means the one is left out of the comedian's name

parts.note: Ernie Wise was a British comedian, of Morecambe and Wise
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone sensible avoids a single street in the Sussex town of Worthing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wise' is Ernie Wise, of the British TV double act Morecambe and Wise. 'Worthing' is not the seaside town but Jack Worthing of The Importance of Being Earnest, who calls himself by this name in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilde's Jack Worthing goes by this alias in town, the joke of The Importance of Being Earnest.

clue.text: Garment that is put on a poet

indicators.note: put on means the second piece is placed after the first

parts.note: Thomas Hood was an English poet
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A piece of clothing is draped over a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Garment' and 'poet' both tempt a solver toward a well-known verse-writer's clothing; Thomas Hood is a nineteenth-century English poet, best known for The Song of the Shirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A hooded sweatshirt is an item of clothing.

clue.text: Pay cut leads to Italian nobles owing Antonio's friend

indicators.note: cut means the pay is shortened, losing its last letter

parts.note: salary means pay

indicators.note: leads to points to the first letters of the three words that follow

explanation.surface: A pay cut leaves Italian aristocrats in debt to a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims SALARY to SALAR; 'leads to' adds INO. In The Merchant of Venice, Salarino is one of Antonio's companions.
explanation.definitionFit: Salarino is one of the Venetian companions of Antonio in The Merchant of Venice.
